title: Quantum entropy inequalities beyond strong subadditivity
formal:
Is there an unconditional homogeneous linear inequality for finite-dimensional quantum subsystem entropies that does not follow from the standard von Neumann inequalities? Precisely, do there exist an integer \(n\ge4\), real coefficients \((c_J)_{\varnothing
e J\subseteq[n]}\), and a vector \(v\in\mathcal V_n\), as defined below, such that \[\sum_{\varnothing
e J\subseteq[n]}c_J S(ho_J)\ge0\] for every choice of finite local dimensions and every \(n\)-party density matrix \(ho\), while \[\sum_{\varnothing
e J\subseteq[n]}c_Jv_J<0?\] The same coefficients must work in every local dimension. The party count is any one finite \(n\ge4\); the target is not restricted to exactly four parties or to a special class of states.
why: This asks whether the established linear laws of quantum entropy are complete. A new unconditional inequality would reveal a universal restriction on sharing quantum information; completeness would characterize every finite-party entropy cone by finitely many standard inequalities, after taking closure.
status_note: Source-open. On 16 September 2026 the full relevant definitions and open-question passages of TQC 2013, the 2025 Quantum Entropy Prover introduction and cone framework, and the revised 2026 holographic-cone §2.1 were checked with current arXiv records and a bounded later-work search. These sources retain the unconditional general quantum entropy cone question. No universal inequality outside the standard cone or proof of equality in every party count was identified. Restricted-state and constrained inequalities are different targets. No cited proof was independently verified or formalized in Lean.

sentences: For a multipartite quantum state, the entropies of all subsystems form a vector subject to universal inequalities.
Positivity and strong subadditivity give basic constraints on those vectors.
This question asks whether additional inequalities are needed to describe the quantum entropy cone for four or more parties.
The cited stabilizer-state analysis relates the problem to classical non-Shannon inequalities and to states violating the Ingleton inequality.
New constraints or counterexamples would sharpen the mathematical description of how quantum information can be shared among several systems.

definitions:
Write \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Choose arbitrary positive integers \(d_1,\ldots,d_n\) and the Hilbert space \(\mathcal H=\bigotimes_{i=1}^n\mathbb C^{d_i}\), with its standard product basis. A density matrix is a Hermitian matrix \(\rho=\rho^\dagger\) that is positive semidefinite, meaning \(z^\dagger\rho z\ge0\) for every complex vector \(z\), and has trace one. Dagger denotes conjugate transpose and trace is the sum of diagonal entries. Arbitrary complex matrix entries and mixed states are allowed.

For a subset \(J\subseteq[n]\), the marginal \(\rho_J\) is obtained by tracing out its complement. In product-basis indices its entries are \[(\rho_J)_{a,b}=\sum_z\rho_{(a,z),(b,z)},\] where \(a,b\) index the factors in \(J\), \(z\) ranges over all basis indices of the complementary factors, and the tuples are placed in the original order of the parties. If \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_D\) are the eigenvalues of a density matrix, define its von Neumann entropy in bits by \(S=-\sum_{j=1}^D\lambda_j\log_2\lambda_j\), with \(0\log_2 0=0\). Define the empty-system entropy to be zero. The entropy vector \(s(\rho)\in\mathbb R^{2^n-1}\) has coordinates \(s(\rho)_J=S(\rho_J)\), indexed by the nonempty subsets.

The standard comparison cone \(\mathcal V_n\) consists of all real vectors \(v=(v_J)_{\varnothing\ne J\subseteq[n]}\), extended by \(v_\varnothing=0\), that satisfy \(v_J\ge0\) for every \(J\), and, for every pair of subsets \(A,B\subseteq[n]\), both \[v_A+v_B\ge v_{A\cap B}+v_{A\cup B}\qquad\text{(strong subadditivity)}\] and \[v_A+v_B\ge v_{A\setminus B}+v_{B\setminus A}\qquad\text{(weak monotonicity)}.\] Disjoint, overlapping, equal and empty subsets are all included. Thus familiar subadditivity and the Araki–Lieb inequalities are already among the consequences. Weak monotonicity follows from strong subadditivity after purifying a quantum state with an additional party; it is explicitly included here so it cannot be counted as a new inequality. Every actual quantum entropy vector lies in \(\mathcal V_n\), but a vector in this cone is only a list of real numbers and is not promised to come from a state.

An inequality is homogeneous linear if its left side is the displayed linear combination with constant coefficients and zero right side. It is unconditional if it holds for all states and dimensions, without extra entropy equalities, independence assumptions or a restriction to stabilizer, classical or holographic states. Not following from the standard inequalities means exactly that it fails at some vector of \(\mathcal V_n\), as required by the strict inequality in the target. This is semantic nonimplication; no choice of syntactic proof system is involved. Equivalently, since the closure of the set of quantum entropy vectors is a closed convex cone, the question asks whether this closure is strictly smaller than \(\mathcal V_n\) for at least one finite \(n\ge4\). Closure means approximation to arbitrary accuracy in the finite-dimensional real coordinate space; it is not exact realization by a single finite-dimensional state. No running-time or algorithmic discovery requirement is imposed.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the stated existence, including validity for every finite-dimensional state and an exact vector witnessing nonimplication by the standard cone, or a complete Lean-checked proof of its logical negation. The negative outcome must show that for every finite \(n\ge4\), every universally valid homogeneous linear entropy inequality is nonnegative on every vector in \(\mathcal V_n\). Equivalently it proves equality of the closed quantum entropy cone and \(\mathcal V_n\) for every such \(n\). A positive outcome needs only one party count, but a negative result for exactly four parties does not settle all larger counts. An inequality valid under additional constraints, a restriction to some states, or failure of exact realization of a boundary vector without excluding arbitrarily close realizations does not establish the requested separation. Numerical searches alone and approximate versions of the strict separation are insufficient.

context_blocks.text: A multipartite state has one entropy for every nonempty subsystem. Universal linear inequalities limit which patterns of shared quantum information are possible, independently of the dimensions used to realize them. The question asks whether the familiar inequalities already exhaust these linear constraints.

Quantum entropy differs from classical entropy: adjoining a system can reduce entropy. For instance, a pure maximally entangled pair has zero joint entropy and positive one-party entropies. Classical monotonicity cannot be added to the comparison cone; the source uses weak monotonicity instead.

For at most three parties, the closure of the set of quantum entropy vectors is characterized by the standard inequalities. For four or more, the source explicitly distinguishes this closed-cone question from the exact set of realizable entropy vectors. Nonrealizability at a limiting boundary point alone is not a new universal linear inequality.

Classical non-Shannon inequalities demonstrate that the analogous classical outer cone is too large. That fact does not transfer directly to quantum states, because classical diagonal states form only a subclass and quantum conditional entropy can be negative.

The 2013 paper characterizes the four-party stabilizer entropy cone using an additional Ingleton inequality. General quantum states, including some classical diagonal states, need not satisfy Ingleton. The theorem therefore answers a restricted-state question and leaves the target here open.

Known constrained quantum entropy inequalities assume additional relations among entropies. Such a conclusion can fail to survive limits of states that only approach those relations. It does not automatically give an unconditional separating inequality for the closed entropy cone.

The 2025 Quantum Entropy Prover formalizes deduction from strong subadditivity and weak monotonicity using linear programming, and also handles supplied constraints. Its introduction explicitly retains existence of non-von-Neumann-type unconditional inequalities as an open question; an automated prover for the known cone does not characterize the actual quantum cone.

The 2026 holographic-cone paper also distinguishes the unresolved general quantum cone from the more restricted holographic setting. New graph realizations or inequalities for that restricted cone do not apply to every finite-dimensional quantum state.
